relevance_score_definition: 0 < x <= 1, with a higher score indicating higher relevance.

feed.title: The semiconductor decade: A trillion-dollar industry
feed.summary: The global semiconductor industry is projected to reach a trillion-dollar valuation by 2030, driven by an average annual growth rate of 6 to 8 percent. Key growth areas include automotive, computation and data storage, and wireless technologies, with automotive expected to triple demand. Industry leaders are advised to strategically focus on R&D, manufacturing, and sourcing to capitalize on this expansion.

feed.title: TSMC To Become NVIDIA’s Sole GPU Supplier In 2022 – Report
feed.summary: A report from Business Korea suggests that TSMC is poised to become NVIDIA's sole GPU supplier by the end of 2022 due to ongoing issues with Samsung Foundry's production yields. NVIDIA, which previously diversified its suppliers, is now reportedly moving all its GPU manufacturing to TSMC, including its new Hopper data center GPUs. This shift follows earlier rumors of a rift between Samsung and NVIDIA and significant investments by NVIDIA into TSMC's advanced manufacturing processes.

feed.title: Corsair One i300 review
feed.summary: The Corsair One i300 is a compact and stylish small form factor gaming PC that offers extremely high-end performance with components like the Intel Core i9-12900K and Nvidia GeForce RTX 3080 Ti. While it excels in performance for 4K gaming and also serves as a powerful workstation for content creators, its major drawbacks are its exorbitant price tag ($4,999 / £4,399) and limited upgradeability due to its small chassis. The review concludes that while it's a top-tier machine for those who can afford it and don't plan on tinkering, it's overkill and too expensive for most casual gamers.

feed.title: Investing in esports in the context of recent events
feed.summary: This article discusses the growth of esports, significant investment it has received, and current challenges due to global events like the COVID-19 pandemic and the Russia-Ukraine conflict. It identifies investment opportunities in publicly traded tech companies, specialized esports firms, and esports-focused ETFs, while also raising questions about future growth amidst potential new pandemics and the integration of NFTs.

feed.title: Baidu Proposes PP-YOLOE: An Evolved Version of YOLO that Achieves SOTA Performance in Object Detection
feed.summary: Baidu researchers have introduced PP-YOLOE, an evolved version of the YOLO object detector, which demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in object detection. This new model surpasses previous versions like YOLOX and PP-YOLOv2 in both speed and accuracy on COCO datasets. The improvements stem from architectural optimizations, an anchor-free method, novel RepResBlock usage, task alignment learning, and an Efficient Task-aligned Head.

feed.title: New IBM Z mainframe blunts quantum cyber attacks
feed.summary: IBM has introduced its latest Z mainframe system, featuring a new Telum processor with a built-in AI accelerator. This system is designed to enhance AI inferencing capabilities for financial transactions, enabling real-time fraud analysis. Additionally, it incorporates advanced security measures, including quantum-safe cryptography, to defend against cyberattacks from quantum computers.

feed.title: Technology ETF
feed.summary: VanEck offers a suite of Technology ETFs that allow investors to gain exposure to disruptive and transformative megatrends such as semiconductors, spatial technology, hydrogen, esports, and cryptocurrency. These ETFs provide diversified exposure, potential for future winners through rules-based selection, regular rebalancing, and lower fees compared to actively managed funds. The article also details various risks associated with investing in Technology ETFs, including industry concentration, market risk, and liquidity risks.

feed.title: Hello FPGA – Getting Started with Microchip FPGAs
feed.summary: The "Hello FPGA" webinar introduces Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) and Microchip's low-power FPGA portfolio, drawing from a Microchip University course. It covers fundamental FPGA technology, provides background information, and features videos from the course, guided by Tim McCarthy (Microchip) and Clemens Valens (Elektor). The webinar aims to make FPGAs more accessible, despite their perceived complexity requiring hardware description languages like VHDL or Verilog.

feed.title: Experts Details: Lillian Currens
feed.summary: This page provides details about Lillian Currens, the deputy editor at Schaeffer's Investment Research. It highlights her professional background, experience in writing and editing digital content, and her role in managing Schaeffer's social media. The article also lists several of her published articles discussing stock analyses for companies like Netflix, Vertex Pharmaceuticals, Nvidia, and Home Depot.

feed.title: Meta (FB) Plans to Introduce Virtual Coins to Diversify Income
feed.summary: Meta Platforms (FB) is exploring the introduction of virtual coins, tokens, and lending services within its applications to reduce its reliance on advertising revenue. The company plans to create in-app tokens, similar to those in games like Roblox, and also social tokens and "creator coins" for influencers, rather than a blockchain-based cryptocurrency like its failed Diem project. This strategic shift aims to diversify its income streams and engage users amidst increasing competition and regulatory scrutiny.

feed.title: Which is the bigger company: AMD, Nvidia, or Intel?
feed.summary: This article analyzes Intel, AMD, and Nvidia to determine which is the "bigger" company, looking beyond market capitalization to factors like employee count, revenue, product diversity, and market share. While Nvidia leads in market cap, sustained analysis reveals Intel to be the largest overall due to its revenue and employee numbers, despite AMD and Nvidia's significant recent growth. The article also touches on the unique advantage Intel holds with its chip manufacturing capabilities.

feed.title: Metaverse Market Size [2022-2029] Worth USD 1527.55 Billion | Exhibiting a CAGR of 47.6%
feed.summary: The metaverse market is projected to grow significantly from USD 100.27 billion in 2022 to USD 1,527.55 billion by 2029, showcasing a CAGR of 47.6%. This growth is primarily driven by the increasing penetration of online shopping and gaming, alongside advancements in blockchain technology and VR devices. Key companies leading this expansion include Tencent Holdings Ltd., NVIDIA Corporation, Meta, and Microsoft Corporation, who are focusing on product portfolio expansion and technological innovation.

feed.title: NVIDIA enters Top 5 of Fortune's '100 Best Companies to Work For'
feed.summary: NVIDIA has been ranked #5 on Fortune's 2022 list of the "100 Best Companies to Work For," placing ahead of major financial institutions like Capital One and American Express. Cisco secured the top spot for the second consecutive year, followed by Hilton and Wegmans Food Markets, Inc., with Salesforce coming in fourth. The recognition highlights the importance of strong workplace culture during a period of significant workforce changes.

feed.title: These 4 Houston companies are honored as Fortune’s 100 Best Companies to Work For
feed.summary: Four Houston-based companies, including David Weekley Homes, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Camden Property Trust, and Hilcorp, have been recognized on Fortune's 2022 100 Best Companies to Work For list. David Weekley Homes notably secured a top 10 spot, ranking No. 9, while other Texas companies also made the list. The rankings were determined by Great Place to Work, surveying employees on trust, care, and fairness.

feed.title: Ensuring a stronger US-Taiwan tech supply chain partnership
feed.summary: This article discusses the importance of strengthening the US-Taiwan tech supply chain partnership, particularly in the semiconductor industry, amidst increasing global geopolitical polarization. It highlights the challenges of meeting chip demands, cultivating engineering talent, and the need for comprehensive integration beyond just manufacturing. The piece advocates for policy clarity, R&D collaborations, and deeper economic integration to ensure mutual benefit and resilience for both the US and Taiwan.

feed.title: The end of one-chip wonders: Why Nvidia, Intel and AMD's valuations have experienced massive upheaval
feed.summary: The semiconductor industry has seen a dramatic shift, with Nvidia now valued as much as Intel and AMD combined, a reversal from five years ago when Intel held that position. This change reflects evolving technology interaction and other companies specializing in new areas, causing Intel to fall behind. The article highlights a massive upheaval in semiconductor valuations mirroring the industry's transformation.

feed.title: The end of one-chip wonders: Why Nvidia, Intel and AMD’s valuations have experienced massive upheaval
feed.summary: The article discusses the dramatic shift in valuations among semiconductor companies, specifically Nvidia, Intel, and AMD. Five years ago, Intel's market capitalization surpassed Nvidia and AMD combined, but now Nvidia alone is worth more than the other two combined, reflecting significant changes in the semiconductor industry. This upheaval is attributed to evolving technology consumption patterns and companies specializing in new areas.

feed.title: The end of one-chip wonders: Why Nvidia, Intel and AMD’s valuations have experienced massive upheaval
feed.summary: This article discusses the dramatic shift in market capitalization within the semiconductor industry over the past five years. Once dominant Intel has been surpassed by Nvidia, which is now valued as much as Intel and AMD combined, reflecting fundamental changes in how technology is used and specialized solutions. This upheaval highlights a significant transformation in the industry's landscape.

feed.title: Micron Commences Volume Production of 16 Gb GDDR6X Memory For NVIDIA’s RTX 3090 Ti, Also Readies 24 Gbps GDDR6X Dies For Future Graphics Cards
feed.summary: Micron has begun volume production of its 16Gb GDDR6X memory, which is now integrated into NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 3090 Ti graphics card, offering twice the capacity and up to 15% higher performance than its predecessor. The company is also developing 24 Gbps GDDR6X memory dies to enhance performance in future graphics cards, supporting speeds up to 24Gb/s. This advancement leverages Micron's PAM4 signal techniques for improved power efficiency and bandwidth, critical for demanding applications like 4K/8K gaming and 3D CAD.

feed.title: With Vast Data, Nvidia is in the company of a storage unicorn
feed.summary: Nvidia has deepened its relationship with storage unicorn Vast Data, with Nvidia Bluefield DPUs now powering Vast Data's new Ceres storage platform. This collaboration aims to redefine data center storage for the AI era by leveraging advanced flash drives and DPU technology for improved performance and cost efficiency. The partnership evolved through Mellanox, which Nvidia acquired and had previously invested in Vast Data, and both companies are also developing Zero Trust access to data storage and GPU direct storage.

feed.title: Broadcom Inc. stock falls Thursday, underperforms market
feed.summary: Broadcom Inc. (AVGO) stock fell 3.15% on Thursday, closing at $573.85, a day when the broader market also saw declines. This drop ended a two-day winning streak for the company, leaving its stock $103.91 short of its 52-week high. Competitors such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd. ADR, NVIDIA Corp., and Intel Corp. also experienced declines.

feed.title: Synopsys Introduces Industry's Highest Performance Neural Processor IP
feed.summary: Synopsys has launched its DesignWare ARC NPX6 and NPX6FS NPU IP, along with the MetaWare MX Development Toolkit, to meet the increasing performance demands of AI systems-on-chip. This new NPU IP delivers the industry's highest performance, offering up to 3,500 TOPS for AI applications and support for complex neural network models, while also addressing functional safety requirements for automotive use. The comprehensive software environment aims to accelerate application development and ensure compliance with standards like ISO 26262.

feed.title: Nvidia's GPU-powered AI is creating chips with 'better than human design'
feed.summary: Nvidia is leveraging its GPU-powered AI to develop and design new computer chips, including its own GPUs, leading to designs that are "better than human." The company's chief scientist, Bill Dally, explained how AI is used to accelerate chip design processes like power estimation, parasitic prediction, and automated standard cell migration. This approach not only significantly reduces design time and labor but also results in more efficient and smaller chip components, showcasing a win-win scenario for Nvidia's internal development and its AI hardware offerings.

feed.summary: The Roundhill Cannabis ETF (BATS:WEED) is an actively managed exchange-traded fund that invests in global cannabis and hemp companies. feed.title: Lapsus$ Cyberattack Victim List: Globant, Microsoft, Nvidia, Okta, Samsung, T-Mobile -
feed.summary: The Lapsus$ hacker group continued to target high-profile companies even after some alleged members were arrested in March 2022. This article lists several major companies, including Globant, Microsoft, Nvidia, Okta, Samsung, and T-Mobile, that have been victims of Lapsus$ cyberattacks. It also provides guidance on how to protect against and respond to ransomware attacks, emphasizing data backups, multi-factor authentication, and prompt incident reporting.

feed.title: Leaked Chats Show LAPSUS$ Stole T-Mobile Source Code – Krebs on Security
feed.summary: Leaked private chat messages from the LAPSUS$ cybercrime group reveal they breached T-Mobile multiple times in March 2022, stealing source code for various projects. Despite T-Mobile's claim that no customer or government information was compromised, the chats detail LAPSUS$'s methods, including purchasing access, social engineering employees, and utilizing internal tools like Atlas to look up sensitive accounts. The article also highlights the group's internal conflicts, their leader's fixation on stealing source code, and their eventual undoing due to compromised servers and arrests.

feed.title: Chipmaker Texas Instruments expects revenue hit as China lockdowns dent demand
feed.summary: Texas Instruments (TXN.O) forecast second-quarter revenue below Wall Street estimates due to reduced demand caused by COVID-19 lockdowns in China, sending its shares down 7% in extended trading. The company noted that the impact was primarily due to disruptions at its customers' factories. Despite this, Texas Instruments reported a 14% revenue increase to $4.91 billion for the first quarter, exceeding analyst expectations.

feed.title: Fidelity Enters the Metaverse with New Financial Education Experience: Invest Quest at The Fidelity Stack
feed.summary: Fidelity Investments has launched a new gamified financial education experience called "The Fidelity Stack" in Decentraland, an eight-story virtual building designed to teach users about ETF investing through an "Invest Quest" challenge. This initiative aims to engage younger audiences, particularly the 18-35 age range, following the company's recent introduction of a metaverse-themed ETF, FMET. Fidelity views this as a significant step in providing financial education in decentralized, virtual communities.

feed.title: HPE Creates Its Own AI Stack For Large Enterprises
feed.summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is expanding its AI software portfolio and leveraging its HPC hardware expertise to provide a comprehensive AI stack for large enterprises. This initiative includes a Machine Learning Development System that simplifies infrastructure management and facilitates collaboration for training models at scale, addressing the complexities faced by data scientists. Furthermore, HPE is promoting "swarm learning" to enable AI model training where data resides, crucial for privacy and compliance in industries like healthcare and banking.

feed.title: HCL Technologies brings All Access Media Marketplace Platform
feed.summary: HCL Technologies has launched its All Access Media Marketplace Platform at NAB Las Vegas, aiming to streamline content creation and distribution processes. Developed in coordination with Microsoft and CoreSite, the platform addresses workflow, application, and vendor discovery challenges for media creators. It features HCL Workflow Creator for building workflows, leverages Microsoft 365 for communication, and utilizes Azure Cloud for cybersecurity, aligning with MovieLabs 2030 Vision.

feed.title: Nvidia’s CFO on how they retain tech talent —even as the Great Resignation continues
feed.summary: Colette Kress, Nvidia's CFO, discusses the company's strategies for retaining top tech talent amidst the Great Resignation. She emphasizes that beyond competitive salaries, a strong culture focused on continuous learning, challenging work, and an egalitarian leadership approach are key factors. Nvidia provides unique upskilling opportunities, offers benefits like "Free Days" and an employee stock purchase program, and fosters an environment where all employees are valued and have opportunities to lead, regardless of title.

feed.title: US-based Applied Materials’ India arm buys office space, land in Bangalore for Rs 338 crore
feed.summary: Applied Materials India, the subsidiary of the US-based semiconductor equipment manufacturer, has acquired nearly 10 acres of land and 2.6 lakh sq ft of office space in Bangalore for Rs 338 crore. This acquisition is part of the company's plan to invest over Rs 1,800 crore in India to expand its engineering infrastructure and support its growth. India is projected to become the fastest-growing semiconductor consumption market globally, with demand expected to exceed $110 billion by the end of the decade.

feed.title: “There must be a new approach to the design of chips for high-performance computing applications”
feed.summary: Joe Costello, former CEO of Cadence, has joined Anari AI as a Board Advisor to guide the startup in revolutionizing the hardware AI industry. Costello discusses the future of semiconductors, emphasizing the transition from general-purpose to domain-specific architectures, the critical role of cloud computing, and the transformative impact of AI/ML. He highlights the necessity of new chip design approaches for high-performance computing and the importance of fostering strong ecosystems.

feed.title: Nvidia: transforming industries with pioneering AI tech
feed.summary: Nvidia, a leader in AI and accelerated computing, is transforming industries through its pioneering technology. The company designs GPUs and APIs, supporting over 2.5 million developers globally and expanding its presence in gaming with RTX technology. Nvidia has also developed the Omniverse platform for virtual world simulation and is rapidly advancing supercomputing with its CUDA programming model and new H100 GPU and Grace CPU Superchip processors.

feed.title: FMET Is a New, Fabulous Metaverse Idea
feed.summary: Fidelity has launched the Fidelity Metaverse ETF (FMET), which tracks the Fidelity Metaverse Index, to capitalize on the nascent but expanding metaverse investment theme. The ETF mixes established tech giants with innovative smaller companies, including Meta Platforms, Apple, NVIDIA, Tencent, Baidu, and JD.com. Investors are advised that patience will be key for metaverse investing due to anticipated volatility, though the long-term growth outlook is considered bright with billions in projected revenue.

feed.title: Toyota to apply artificial intelligence to boost efficiency in its factories
feed.summary: Toyota Motor North America (TMNA) is partnering with Invisible AI to implement artificial intelligence in its factories to improve efficiency and safety. This AI system, using computer vision, will be deployed in 14 North American factories to analyze manufacturing operations, detect issues, and enhance processes. The initiative aims to reduce inefficiencies and ensures data privacy by analyzing information in-house and anonymizing videos to protect workers.

feed.title: Nvidia fined $5.5M by SEC over failing to disclose crypto as revenue generator
feed.summary: Nvidia has been fined $5.5 million by the SEC for failing to disclose that cryptomining was a significant revenue generator from its graphics processing units designed for gaming. The SEC stated that Nvidia deprived investors of critical information regarding the impact of volatile cryptocurrency sales on its business. Nvidia did not admit or deny the findings and has agreed to a cease-and-desist order.

feed.title: Nvidia to pay $5.5 million penalty for 'inadequate disclosures' about cryptomining
feed.summary: Nvidia Corporation has agreed to pay a $5.5 million civil penalty to settle charges from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The SEC alleged that Nvidia failed to adequately disclose the significant impact of cryptomining on its gaming revenue growth in fiscal 2018. The company did not admit or deny the findings but agreed to the settlement, which highlights its omission of information crucial for investors and analysts.

feed.title: Nvidia pays $5.5m SEC fine over crypto-mining disclosures
feed.summary: Nvidia agreed to pay a $5.5 million fine to the SEC for failing to adequately disclose revenue from crypto mining during two quarters in 2018. The SEC stated that Nvidia omitted information about surging demand from crypto miners while discussing how digital assets impacted other business lines. This lack of disclosure made Nvidia's financial results less predictable for investors.

feed.title: Nvidia To Pay $5.5M Fine For Failing To Disclose GPU Cryptomining Sales: SEC
feed.summary: Nvidia has been fined $5.5 million by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for failing to disclose to investors that a significant portion of its 2018 GPU sales were driven by cryptocurrency mining. The SEC alleged that Nvidia misled investors and analysts, who were keenly interested in the impact of crypto mining on the company's gaming revenue. While Nvidia didn't admit wrongdoing, it agreed to pay the civil penalty.

feed.title: NVIDIA (NVDA) Fined $5.5M for Failing to Disclose Crypto Mining Impact
feed.summary: NVIDIA was fined $5.5 million by the SEC for failing to disclose the significant impact of cryptocurrency mining demand on its graphics card sales during fiscal year 2018. The SEC stated that this omission deprived investors of crucial information regarding the company's business in a key market. Following the settlement, NVIDIA's stock experienced a decline, reflecting the underperformance of its crypto mining processor (CMP) chips amid a downturn in cryptocurrency prices.

feed.title: Why Marvell bought interconnect upstart Tanzanite
feed.summary: Marvell Technology has acquired Tanzanite, a CXL startup specializing in memory expansion and pooling, to accelerate its composable infrastructure ambitions. The acquisition aims to disaggregate compute, memory, and storage resources, allowing them to be composed on the fly for memory-intensive workloads like AI/ML. While achieving fully composable data centers will take time, Marvell believes CXL technology will be crucial for integrating accelerators across its product portfolio and overcoming latency challenges associated with extending CXL benefits beyond server chassis.

feed.title: NetApp Teams with NVIDIA to Accelerate HPC and AI with Turnkey Supercomputing Infrastructure
feed.summary: NetApp and NVIDIA announced an expanded AI portfolio, including the certification of NetApp EF600 all-flash NVMe storage with BeeGFS file system for NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD. This partnership aims to simplify AI and HPC infrastructure, offering solutions like ONTAP AI and NVIDIA DGX Foundry to provide turnkey supercomputing capabilities. The collaboration provides organizations with flexible, high-performance infrastructure for AI development, whether on-premises or as a hosted service.

feed.title: Intel launches new AI chips, challenging Nvidia's market
feed.summary: Intel Corp launched new AI chips, Gaudi2 and Greco, to challenge Nvidia's dominance in the AI chip market. The company is focusing on developing its open-standard software platform to differentiate itself and aims to capture a significant share of the rapidly growing AI chip market, estimated to reach $50 billion in the next five years.

feed.title: Qualcomm Inc. stock underperforms Tuesday when compared to competitors despite daily gains
feed.summary: Qualcomm Inc. (QCOM) stock rose 1.40% on Tuesday, closing at $136.81, despite a mixed trading session for the broader market. This gain, however, meant the stock underperformed some competitors like Alphabet Inc. and NVIDIA Corp., and remained significantly below its 52-week high.

feed.title: TSMC plans another price hike amid inflation concerns
feed.summary: TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, is reportedly planning to raise prices again by single-digit percentages. This marks the second price increase in less than a year, attributed to rising inflation, escalating costs, and the company's extensive expansion efforts aimed at addressing the global chip shortage.

feed.title: Absci Reports First Quarter 2022 Financial and Operating Results
feed.summary: Absci Corporation announced its first-quarter 2022 financial and operating results, highlighting significant progress in advancing partnered programs, securing new collaborations, and enhancing its AI-driven technology platform. The company reported a net loss of $29.5 million and cash and cash equivalents of $226.0 million, sufficient to fund operations through the end of 2024, while reiterating its guidance for at least eight new Active Programs in 2022. Key achievements include a research collaboration with Merck, machine learning breakthroughs for antibody discovery, and a partnership with NVIDIA.

feed.title: Improving PPA With AI
feed.summary: This article discusses how Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are increasingly being used in Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools to enhance chip design by improving Power, Performance, and Area (PPA), reducing design errors, and accelerating time to market. It highlights that while AI can't replace the need for human designers to make critical decisions, it significantly streamlines tedious processes and optimizes designs that would be too complex for humans alone. The integration of AI promises greater efficiency, cost reduction, and the ability to design highly complex chips, as demonstrated by examples from leading technology companies.

feed.title: Z by HP Powers Today’s Professionals to Create without Limitation
feed.summary: HP announced new Z by HP solutions, including ZBook mobile workstations, Z displays, a Thunderbolt G4 Dock, and tools for data scientists, aimed at empowering creative and technical professionals. These products offer enhanced performance, seamless collaboration, and improved productivity for those working in diverse environments, from on-the-go to hybrid setups. Key features include powerful CPUs/GPUs, high-refresh-rate displays, secure docking, and a new Data Science Stack Manager to streamline workflows.

feed.title: Intel wants to add a new Licking County factory "every year or two," CEO says
feed.summary: Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger announced plans to open a new factory in Licking County "every year or two" as part of a $100 billion investment to make the area a major semiconductor hub. This ambitious expansion hinges on Congress passing the $52 billion CHIPS Act, which Gelsinger deems essential for competitive U.S. chip manufacturing. The project aims to rebuild the U.S. semiconductor sector and will require significant workforce development and sustained support from Ohio.

feed.title: Gina Sanchez explains why these two mega cap stocks are a buy
feed.summary: Gina Sanchez, chief market strategist at Lido Advisors, recommends buying Walmart Inc (NYSE: WMT) and Nvidia Corporation (NASDAQ: NVDA) stocks. She believes Walmart is a strong reopening stock capable of handling supply chain issues, while Nvidia offers a deep discount opportunity as a leader in the semiconductor space, essential for the growing Cloud trend. Both companies are scheduled to report their quarterly results later this month.

feed.title: Pure Storage, Snowflake partner on analyzing local data
feed.summary: Pure Storage and Snowflake have partnered to enable data analytics on Pure's on-premises FlashBlade storage using Snowflake's Data Cloud capabilities. This collaboration allows customers to analyze large local datasets without moving them to the cloud, addressing data control and migration challenges. The partnership leverages Amazon S3 and aims to provide hybrid cloud advantages for analytical workloads, with the public preview expected later this year.

feed.title: Broom, Broom: WeRide Revs Up Self-Driving Street Sweepers Powered by NVIDIA
feed.summary: WeRide has launched a public pilot of 50 self-driving Robo Street Sweepers in Guangzhou, China, powered by NVIDIA technology. These vehicles perform essential municipal cleaning services autonomously, leveraging NVIDIA's high-performance AI compute platform for real-time data processing and safety. This deployment marks WeRide's second mass-produced self-driving vehicle and expands its diverse fleet of autonomous solutions.

feed.title: Top blockchain stocks to explore: COIN, SQ, NVDA, MARA & RIOT
feed.summary: This article highlights several top blockchain stocks, including Coinbase Global, NVIDIA Corporation, and Riot Blockchain. It mentions Coinbase's Q1 FY22 net revenue and NVIDIA's upcoming Q1 FY23 financial results. The content provides a glimpse into the financial performance of these key players in the blockchain sector.

feed.summary: This article explains Syfe's Disruptive Technology portfolio, detailing why investors should consider disruptive tech and how Syfe approaches this investment theme through direct stock holdings rather than ETFs. It outlines six key themes within the portfolio—Blockchain and crypto, Robotics and Artificial Intelligence, Fintech, Next-gen internet, Cloud-computing and cybersecurity, and Video games and e-sports—highlighting top holdings for each. The article emphasizes cost savings for investors through Syfe's direct investment model.

It seeks to adapt to market conditions by adjusting allocations based on price action, volatility, and correlation signals. The fund, launched on May 18, 2022, has an expense ratio of 0.65% and its top holdings include NVIDIA Corporation and Apple Inc.

feed.title: HP Envy 34 All-in-One Desktop review: A big-screen AIO for power users and creators
feed.summary: HP has updated its Envy All-in-One desktop, featuring a 34-inch 5K wide-screen display, making it a strong alternative to the discontinued 27-inch iMac for creative users and power users. This review highlights its impressive design, versatile features including accessible RAM/SSD slots, and strong performance, especially in graphics, though it notes some bloatware and a lack of display swivel. The Envy 34 offers various configurations, from an entry-level model to a high-end option with a Core i9 processor and RTX 3080 graphics.

feed.title: Baidu’s Chip Affiliate Kunlun Eyes Fundraise at $2.5 Billion Valuation
feed.summary: Baidu's chip affiliate, Kunlun, is seeking to raise 2 billion yuan ($317 million) in a new funding round, which would value the company at $2.5 billion. This initiative reflects a trend in China's venture capital landscape, where investors are pivoting from internet businesses towards core technologies like semiconductors, aligning with Beijing's strategic priorities. If successful, this would be Kunlun's second funding round, increasing its valuation significantly from its previous round.

feed.title: TI Breaks Ground on New Semiconductor Wafer Plants in Sherman with Potential $30B Investment
feed.summary: Texas Instruments has broken ground on new 300-mm semiconductor wafer fabrication plants in Sherman, Texas, representing a potential $30 billion investment. This project is the largest private-sector economic development in Texas history, aiming to create up to 3,000 jobs and produce millions of analog and embedded processing chips daily. Production from the first fab is expected to begin in 2025, contributing to long-term manufacturing capacity for semiconductors in the U.S.

feed.title: Wall Street ends sharply lower as Target and growth stocks sink
feed.summary: Wall Street closed sharply lower on Wednesday after Target's stock plummeted by about a quarter of its value, exposing concerns about the U.S. economy due to surging prices. This marked the worst one-day loss for the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average since June 2020, as inflation continued to erode consumer purchasing power, impacting retailers and prompting a market sell-off. Megacap growth stocks also contributed to the decline, with the Nasdaq falling significantly, amidst broader economic worries including rising inflation, supply chain issues, and central bank tightening.

feed.title: 上海汽車、「純中国産」に固執せず自動運転タクシー開発
feed.summary: 中国の上海汽車集団（SAIC）が、自動運転レベル4のロボタクシー車両開発において、アメリカ企業Cerenceの音声AI技術を採用することを発表しました。SAICは「純中国産」にこだわらず、Cerence Mobility PlatformとSpeech Signal Enhancementを導入し、乗客が音声で車内機能を操作できる高精度のロボタクシー実用化を目指しています。これは、NVIDIAの自動運転ソリューション採用に続く、海外技術の積極的な取り入れの一環です。

feed.title: SEI Enhanced U.S. Large Cap Value Factor ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (BATS:SEIV)
feed.summary: The SEI Enhanced U.S. Large Cap Value Factor ETF (SEIV) is an actively managed exchange-traded fund that invests in U.S. large-cap stocks perceived to be undervalued. Launched on May 18, 2022, and managed by SEI, SEIV has assets under management of $1.35 billion and a net expense ratio of 0.15%. As of the article's date, SEIV shares were trading at $45.25, reflecting a 9.0% increase year-to-date, and its top holdings include major tech companies like NVIDIA, Alphabet, and Apple.

feed.title: Clorox Stock (CLX): Anything But A Value Stock
feed.summary: This article challenges the traditional classification of Clorox as a "value stock" and Nvidia as a "growth stock" by analyzing their fundamentals and valuations. The author argues that despite Clorox's low-growth industry, its valuation, when considering metrics like the PEG ratio and a proprietary model, makes it less of a value than commonly perceived. Conversely, Nvidia, a high-growth company, appears more reasonably valued than Clorox when growth prospects are factored in.

feed.title: Semiconductor Competition: Opportunities for Taiwan
feed.summary: The article discusses how Taiwan, particularly TSMC, dominates the global semiconductor industry despite intensifying geopolitical competition and efforts by countries like the US, EU, and China to achieve self-sufficiency in chip manufacturing. It highlights Taiwan's current technological edge and suggests that rather than threats, these global shifts present opportunities for Taiwanese firms to expand into new markets, enhance R&D, and diversify their economic reliance on manufacturing through strategic international partnerships.

feed.title: Taiwan’s Tech Titans Adopt World’s First NVIDIA Grace CPU-Powered System Designs
feed.summary: NVIDIA announced that major Taiwanese computer makers like ASUS, Foxconn Industrial Internet, GIGABYTE, QCT, Supermicro, and Wiwynn will release the first systems powered by the NVIDIA Grace CPU Superchip and Grace Hopper Superchip in the first half of 2023. These systems are designed for various demanding workloads including digital twins, AI, high-performance computing, cloud graphics, and gaming. The Grace Superchips deliver advanced performance and energy efficiency, supporting NVIDIA's vision of "AI factories" in data centers.

feed.title: Nvidia Q1 FY2023 Earnings Report Preview: What To Look For
feed.summary: Nvidia (NVDA) is set to report Q1 FY 2023 earnings, with analysts expecting growth in adjusted EPS and revenue, albeit at a slower pace. Investors will closely watch data center revenue, which is projected to accelerate and potentially surpass gaming revenue for the first time in FY 2023. The company is investing in AI chips to continue its growth trajectory, building on demand fueled by the pandemic.

feed.title: Semiconductor ETF | ESG-screened investment in tech
feed.summary: The VanEck Semiconductor UCITS ETF offers investors exposure to the semiconductor sector, targeting pure-play companies with at least half their revenues from semiconductors. It is Europe's first Semiconductor ETF, designed to capture growth from the "fourth industrial revolution" driven by semiconductor advancements, and is classified as SFDR Article 8 for promoting environmental and social characteristics. The ETF focuses on liquid semiconductor stocks globally and has a strategy that has been successful in the US since 2011, with $25 billion in AUM.

feed.title: The Next $1 Trillion US Tech Stock Is Far Away From Joining Exclusive Club
feed.summary: Nvidia's (NVDA) stock slump has put its $1 trillion valuation on hold, with the company’s stock giving back nearly all its gains from the past year. Investors are keenly awaiting first-quarter earnings to gauge the company's immediate future. The stock's performance has been pressured by factors including lockdowns in China and a general rout in high-valuation stocks.

feed.title: Nvidia stock falls on light guidance, CFO says company will slow hiring
feed.summary: Nvidia's stock dropped after providing a light forecast for the current quarter, despite beating analyst expectations for sales and earnings in Q1 2023. The company announced it would slow hiring and control expenses due to a "challenging macro environment." Revenue for the current quarter is projected to be $8.1 billion, lower than analyst expectations, with the CFO citing the war in Ukraine and Covid lockdowns in China as contributing factors.

feed.title: Texas Instruments Inc. stock rises Wednesday, outperforms market
feed.summary: Texas Instruments Inc. (TXN) stock increased by 1.28% to $170.01 on Wednesday, outperforming the broader market indexes like the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. The company's stock closed $32.25 below its 52-week high, while competitors like NVIDIA Corp. and Qualcomm Inc. also saw gains. Trading volume for Texas Instruments was 4.7 million, which was below its 50-day average.

feed.title: Focus on FMET for Metaverse Equity Bargains
feed.summary: The article suggests that while metaverse equities, being growth stocks, are currently out of favor due to rising interest rates and inflation, they represent a significant long-term disruptive theme. The Fidelity Metaverse ETF (FMET) is highlighted as a way for investors to gain exposure to this trend without the burden of stock picking. BlackRock research indicates growing interest in the metaverse, comparing its current stage to the early days of the internet, and points to opportunities in companies supplying components for VR and AR technologies.

feed.title: Nvidia says video gaming market slowing; shares drop 7%
feed.summary: Nvidia projects a decline in video game chip sales for the current quarter and attributes new supply-chain challenges to China's COVID-19 lockdowns. CEO Jensen Huang stated the gaming market is slowing, leading to a reduction in sales to China. Despite beating first-quarter revenue and earnings estimates, the company's shares dropped 6.7% due to the softer outlook and ongoing market concerns.

feed.title: Where Does the Supply Chain Crisis Stand Now?
feed.summary: The article discusses the ongoing global supply chain crisis, examining its causes, current impact across various sectors like semiconductors, automobiles, industrials, retail, and restaurants, and potential timelines for recovery. It highlights that while some improvements are being seen, new bottlenecks, such as the war in Ukraine and lockdowns in China, continue to pose challenges, pushing companies to adapt strategies like diversifying supply chains and securing long-term contracts.

feed.title: Nvidia Sees Explosive Growth In Data Center, Professional Visualization
feed.summary: Nvidia reported impressive first fiscal quarter 2023 results, with revenue up 46% year-over-year to $8.3 billion, driven significantly by an 83% increase in data center revenue and a 67% increase in professional visualization revenue. CEO Jensen Huang highlighted four key initiatives: ramping next-generation AI infrastructure, launching the Grace CPU, expanding the ORIN robotics processor, and growing software platforms like Nvidia AI and Omniverse. Despite strong earnings that beat analyst expectations, the stock saw a dip in after-hours trading.

feed.title: Ampere Roadmap Has Four Future Arm Server Chips
feed.summary: Ampere Computing has outlined its future Arm server chip roadmap, revealing plans for three new processors beyond the recently announced AmpereOne ("Siryn") chip, extending through 2025. The company emphasizes its agile development approach and customer-driven roadmap, focusing on a continuous cadence of releases rather than yearly changes, with hyperscalers influencing chip features and lifespan. The roadmap details expected advancements in core count, process technology (moving to 5nm and 3nm), memory (DDR5, DDR6), and PCI-Express versions for these upcoming chips, while also hinting at a future shift to chiplet architectures.

feed.title: Top Global Systems Makers Accelerate Adoption of NVIDIA Grace and Grace Hopper
feed.summary: NVIDIA announced that top global computer makers including Atos, Dell Technologies, GIGABYTE, HPE, Inspur, Lenovo, and Supermicro are adopting its new Grace and Grace Hopper superchips to build next-generation servers for AI and HPC workloads. These systems, utilizing the NVIDIA HGX platform, aim to deliver high performance and energy efficiency. Leading supercomputing centers like Los Alamos National Laboratory and the Swiss National Computing Center are among the first to implement these superchips, with systems like Venado expected to exceed 10 exaflops of AI performance.

feed.title: Los Alamos National Laboratory Announces Details Of Supercomputer Collaboration With Nvidia
feed.summary: Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) announced new details of its supercomputer collaboration with Nvidia and HPE, resulting in the "Venado" system. Venado will be the first U.S. customer to receive an Nvidia Grace central processing unit and will utilize a balanced architecture optimized for diverse scientific research, from materials science to power-grid modeling. It represents a significant step in developing a robust software ecosystem and leadership-class computing capabilities for the Laboratory, with delivery expected in 2023.

feed.title: Solving the World’s Biggest Challenges, Together
feed.summary: NVIDIA is launching a new campaign to connect its diverse impacts across various fields, from gaming and AI to scientific research and business innovation. The campaign aims to highlight how NVIDIA's core GPU technology and platforms like CUDA underpin advancements in seemingly disparate areas, fostering a coherent understanding of the company's broad influence. It emphasizes that these technological spillovers are intentional and represent the essence of NVIDIA's mission to solve global challenges collaboratively.

feed.title: Adas/Connected Car - June 2022 v2
feed.summary: The "ADAS/Connected Car - June 2022" report provides an extensive overview of advancements and challenges in advanced driver-assistance systems and connected vehicle technologies. It emphasizes the critical role of edge computing, the integration of AI with radar systems, and the importance of connectivity for enhancing vehicle safety and performance. The report serves as a valuable resource for understanding the current landscape and future evolution of autonomous and connected automotive technology.

feed.title: 6 High-Quality, Undervalued Semiconductor Stocks
feed.summary: Semiconductor stocks have seen significant declines in 2022, creating a strong buying opportunity for long-term investors. Morningstar analysts highlight several high-quality, undervalued semiconductor companies with strong competitive advantages, benefiting from attractive valuations and a long-term demand surge for chips across various industries. The article discusses when the chip shortage might end and the positive long-term outlook for the sector despite potential short-term slowdowns.

feed.title: Nvidia TAO Toolkit update aims to simplify deep learning model development
feed.summary: Nvidia has updated its TAO Toolkit platform to simplify and accelerate deep learning model creation for enterprise applications, making AI development more accessible and less time-consuming. The toolkit now includes new capabilities like "bring your own model weights" and integration with TensorBoard for better visualization, along with the option to deploy as-a-service with REST APIs. While other companies have also worked on simplifying AI pipelines, analysts note that Nvidia's TAO Toolkit, with its low-code nature and pre-trained models, aims to speed up time-to-market for AI models and reduce the need for extensive data science expertise.

feed.title: ASML engineer who fled charges of stealing chip tech is living comfortably in China as CEO of XTAL Inc.
feed.summary: A former ASML engineer, Zongchang Yu, accused of stealing intellectual property, is now serving as CEO of XTAL Inc. in China. Yu founded two companies, XTAL Inc. and DongFang JingYuan Electron, both facing IP theft allegations from ASML. Despite lawsuits and a massive uncollectable fine against XTAL, Yu fled to China and reportedly runs DongFang with government support, benefiting from patents that include the contested OPC software.

feed.title: OpenLight launches as fabless silicon photonics outfit
feed.summary: OpenLight, a new company formed by Synopsys and Juniper Networks, has launched with the goal of accelerating silicon photonics development. The company specializes in integrated on-chip lasers for high-performance photonic integrated circuits, using Tower Semiconductor's PH18DA fabrication process. OpenLight aims to overcome the challenge of integrating laser sources directly onto silicon photonics wafers, reducing costs and improving power efficiency for various applications like data communications, AI, and optical computing.

feed.title: Vision in the Making: Andrew Ng’s Startup Automates Factory Inspection
feed.summary: Andrew Ng's startup, Landing AI, is leveraging his data-centric AI philosophy and NVIDIA GPUs to automate factory inspections, improving efficiency and reducing costs for manufacturers. Their flagship product, LandingLens, helps classify defects in manufacturing processes, as demonstrated by a chip maker client who significantly reduced costs. The company is also developing LandingEdge to bring AI inference directly to the factory floor.

feed.title: TRFK ETF Profile: Dividends, Returns (AMEX:TRFK)
feed.summary: This article provides a detailed profile of the Pacer Data and Digital Revolution ETF (TRFK), listed on the NYSE American. It covers key statistics such as assets under management, dividend yield, expense ratio, and identifies its issuer, inception date, and the index it tracks. The ETF passively invests in companies involved in data use, manipulation, transmission, or storage, primarily in the Electronic Technology and Technology Services sectors, with most assets in North America.

feed.title: Festo Develops With Isaac Sim to Drive Its Industrial Automation
feed.summary: Festo, a German industrial automation company, is using NVIDIA's Isaac Sim, a robotics simulation application built on NVIDIA Omniverse, to develop AI for its future collaborative robots (cobots). The company's AI lab, led by Dionysios Satikidis, is applying principles from game development to robotics simulation, focusing on narrowing the sim-to-real gap and improving perception for real robots by training AI models on synthetic data. Festo is also utilizing Isaac Cortex within Isaac Sim to simplify programming for cobot skills, aiming to make task-aware robot programming as intuitive as programming gaming AIs.

feed.title: TSMC Chairman Mark Liu on the revolution in semiconductors
feed.summary: TSMC Chairman Mark Liu discusses how 5G, A.I., and high-performance computing (HPC) are ushering in a "golden era" for the semiconductor industry. He highlights how continuous innovation, exemplified by the pure-play foundry model pioneered by TSMC, has driven down costs and enabled widespread technological adoption. Liu projects significant growth for the industry, emphasizing the increasing value and omnipresence of semiconductors in modern society and foreseeing their critical role in future applications like VR/AR and personalized medicine.

feed.title: Nvidia’s Data Center Segment Becomes its Biggest Revenue Contributor for Q1 2022
feed.summary: Nvidia's data center segment has surpassed its gaming segment to become the largest revenue contributor for the company in Q1 2022. This shift signifies the growing importance of AI and cloud computing in Nvidia's business model. The article highlights this significant financial performance change for Nvidia.

feed.title: Fortinet (FTNT) to Split Stock in 5 to Attract More Investors
feed.summary: Fortinet (FTNT) announced a five-for-one forward stock split, effective June 22, aiming to make its shares more accessible to employees and retail investors. This move is expected to boost demand and further increase share prices, building on its impressive 710% return over the past five years. Other tech giants like Alphabet, Amazon, and NVIDIA have also recently undertaken stock splits for similar reasons.

feed.title: Is the Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF (METV) Right for You?
feed.summary: The Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF (METV) offers investors diversified exposure to companies benefiting from the metaverse's growth. This article examines METV's top holdings, including Meta Platforms, Nvidia, Roblox, Microsoft, and Autodesk, highlighting their roles in the metaverse ecosystem. It also discusses the fund's expense ratio and the potential market size of the metaverse industry.

feed.title: Fortinet (FTNT) to Split Stock in 5 to Attract More Investors
feed.summary: Fortinet (FTNT) announced a five-for-one forward stock split to make its shares more accessible to employees and retail investors, with stockholder approval scheduled for June 17. If approved, the stock price will drop from approximately $300 to $60 per share. This move follows similar stock splits by other major tech companies like Alphabet, Amazon, and NVIDIA, aiming to boost demand and potentially increase share prices.

feed.title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) Announces the 12 Winners of its 8th Accelerator Program
feed.summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) has announced the 12 winners of its 8th accelerator program, selected from around 50 companies. This program, launched in 2014, provides one year of personalized support, including mentorship from senior HPE managers and access to HPE's ecosystem, for young innovative French companies. The selected companies are primarily focused on responsible digital, artificial intelligence (especially for industry 4.0), health, and cybersecurity.

feed.title: Metaverse Stock Slump Might Be Big Opportunity
feed.summary: Technology stocks, especially those related to the metaverse, are currently underperforming, but some analysts see this as a potential opportunity. The Fidelity Metaverse ETF (FMET) is positioned to benefit if these stocks rebound, with Citi analysts highlighting several key holdings like Meta Platforms, Nvidia, and Apple as having significant metaverse exposure. Citi forecasts the metaverse and Web3 could be worth $13 trillion, suggesting long-term potential for patient investors in this themed ETF.

feed.title: AMD Reveals Roadmap for Zen 4-based laptop CPU, Zen 5, RDNA 3, and RDNA 4
feed.summary: AMD has unveiled its roadmap for upcoming processors and graphics architectures, including the Zen 4-based Ryzen 7000 series, Zen 5, and RDNA 3, with RDNA 4 slated for 2024. The Zen 4 architecture promises significant performance and efficiency gains, competing with Intel's offerings, while Zen 5 will be a ground-up redesign with AI and machine learning enhancements. The RDNA 3 graphics architecture will be chipset-based and on a 5nm architecture, aiming for 50 percent better performance per watt than its predecessor.

feed.title: Power GaN device market growing at 59% CAGR to $2bn in 2027
feed.summary: The power gallium nitride (GaN) device market is projected to grow at a 59% compound annual growth rate (CAGR), from $126 million in 2021 to $2 billion in 2027, according to Yole Développement. This growth is largely driven by the consumer sector, datacom/telecom, and the emerging automotive market. The report also notes dynamic supply chain activity, including new entrants, significant investments, and a steady transition towards 8-inch GaN-on-silicon platforms to reduce manufacturing costs.

feed.title: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. stock underperforms Monday when compared to competitors
feed.summary: Shares of Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) fell 8.26% on Monday, closing at $86.99, amidst a general market downturn with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones also dropping. The stock recorded its seventh consecutive day of losses and underperformed against competitors such as NVIDIA Corp., Intel Corp., and Texas Instruments Inc. Trading volume for AMD was also below its 50-day average.

feed.title: 7 Founder-Led Stocks to Buy and Hold Forever
feed.summary: This article highlights seven founder-led stocks, including Tesla, Nvidia, Salesforce, Blackstone, Steel Dynamics, Block, and Apollo Global Management, that are considered strong long-term buys due to their history of outperformance. The author emphasizes the sustained engagement of founders in their companies and provides a brief overview of each company's financial health, leadership, and recent performance. The piece suggests that founder-led companies tend to outperform those without a founder in the CEO role.

feed.title: Who's growing faster than Nvidia and AMD? Rising datacenter star Marvell
feed.summary: Marvell Technology significantly outpaced other major fabless chip designers like AMD, Nvidia, and Qualcomm in the first quarter, achieving 72% semiconductor revenue growth. This rapid growth was largely driven by its acquisition of Innovium, a switch ASIC business catering to hyperscale data centers. Marvell is strategically shifting its focus from consumer markets to data infrastructure, with datacenter products now accounting for 44% of its total revenue, reinforcing its long-term growth strategy in cloud, 5G, and automotive sectors.

feed.title: All-In-One Financial Services? Vietnam’s MoMo Has a Super-App for That
feed.summary: Vietnam-based fintech company MoMo has developed a super-app providing all-in-one financial services to over 30 million users. The company leverages NVIDIA GPUs and AI, specifically NVIDIA DGX systems, TensorRT, and Triton Inference Server, to enhance its chatbots, eKYC systems, recommendation engines, and credit scoring models. MoMo's use of AI has significantly sped up development, improved performance, and allowed for more accurate risk assessment, with plans to expand into graph neural networks and potentially make traditional credit scores obsolete.

feed.title: $6.5B Texas Instruments Fab Could Be First of Four at Site Totaling $30B
feed.summary: Texas Instruments plans to build up to four semiconductor chip fabrication plants in Sherman, Texas, with the first $6.5 billion fab already under construction and expected to begin production in 2025. The total investment for all four plants could reach nearly $30 billion, supported by significant local incentives. This development is part of a broader U.S. push to increase domestic semiconductor manufacturing amidst global shortages.

feed.title: The King’s Swedish: AI Rewrites the Book in Scandinavia
feed.summary: AI Sweden, in collaboration with NVIDIA, is developing a large language model called GPT-SW3 for Scandinavian languages. This initiative aims to provide a strategic digital asset, enabling citizens, companies, and government agencies to utilize advanced AI for various linguistic tasks. The model, trained on NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD using NVIDIA NeMo Megatron, is intended to inspire entrepreneurship and enhance services across the Nordic region.

feed.title: Power GaN market to hit $2bn in 2027
feed.summary: The power GaN market is projected to reach $2 billion by 2027, driven significantly by consumer products, which are expected to account for 48% of the market. Key growth areas also include datacom/telecom due to stricter regulations and increasing adoption of 48V-Point-Of-Load systems, as well as the automotive sector with GaN finding its way into DC-DC converters and OBCs. The market is also seeing new players, increased investments, and efforts to reduce manufacturing costs through 8-inch wafer capacity expansion and supply chain consolidation.

feed.title: Opinion | Semiconductor Dependency Imperils American Security
feed.summary: The article argues that the U.S.'s heavy reliance on Taiwan for advanced semiconductor manufacturing poses a significant national security risk, particularly in light of potential Chinese dominance. While some question the effectiveness of U.S. subsidies to foster domestic chip leadership, the authors emphasize that reducing dependence on TSMC is crucial to protect America's technology sector and military capabilities. A disruption in Taiwan's chip production could severely impact the U.S.

feed.title: AI in the Big Easy: NVIDIA Research Lets Content Creators Improvise With 3D Objects
feed.summary: NVIDIA Research has developed a new method called NVIDIA 3D MoMa, which allows content creators to quickly import 3D objects into graphics engines for improvisation and modification. This inverse rendering pipeline converts 2D images into editable 3D triangle mesh models within an hour on a single NVIDIA Tensor Core GPU, making them compatible with existing design tools. The technology was showcased using jazz instruments, highlighting its ability to reconstruct objects with accurate materials and lighting for creative workflows in various industries.

feed.title: Nvidia makes big advances in inverse rendering to transform still photos into 3D objects
feed.summary: Nvidia has announced significant progress in "inverse rendering" with its new method, Nvidia 3D MoMa, which uses AI to convert still photos into editable 3D models. This technology allows developers to quickly import objects into graphics engines, modify materials, lighting, and scale, and is expected to benefit industries like gaming, architecture, and design by automating the typically tedious 3D modeling process. The method can reconstruct 3D mesh models, materials, and lighting from images in under an hour, enabling faster creation of virtual and augmented reality applications.

feed.title: These software companies are unsung winners in the semiconductor industry
feed.summary: This article highlights software companies like Synopsys Inc. (SNPS) and Cadence Design Systems Inc. (CDNS) as critical but often overlooked players in the semiconductor industry. These companies provide Electronic Design Automation (EDA) software, which is essential for chip design engineers. Despite the focus on chip giants, these software firms play a crucial role in enabling the broader semiconductor sector, especially amidst ongoing chip shortages.

feed.title: BITI Chart | ProShares Short Bitcoin Strategy ETF
feed.summary: This page provides a live, interactive chart for the ProShares Short Bitcoin Strategy ETF (BITI), allowing users to analyze its performance. The chart offers various customization options and technical indicators to help investors understand price movements. It also includes current market data for BITI, such as its price, daily range, and 52-week range.

feed.title: Teledyne FLIR Object Detection and Tracking Software Accelerates Thermal Camera Integration for ADAS and Autonomous Vehicles
feed.summary: Teledyne FLIR has released Prism AI, a new software framework designed to accelerate the integration of thermal cameras into advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and autonomous vehicles (AV). Prism AI provides classification, object detection, and tracking, featuring visible-and-thermal image fusion and advanced thermal image processing for superior pedestrian and animal detection, especially at night. This software, compatible with Teledyne FLIR thermal cameras, aims to help automotive OEMs improve safety, reduce development costs, and meet regulatory requirements for nighttime pedestrian crash prevention.

feed.title: NYLI Winslow Focused Large Cap Growth ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:IWFG)
feed.summary: The NYLI Winslow Focused Large Cap Growth ETF (IWFG) is an actively managed, non-transparent ETF focused on achieving long-term capital appreciation by investing in US large-cap growth companies. Launched on June 23, 2022, and managed by IndexIQ, the ETF had assets under management of $60.06 million as of July 2, 2026, with a net expense ratio of 0.65%. Its top holdings include major tech companies like NVIDIA, Microsoft, Apple, and Alphabet.

feed.title: 7 Top Metaverse Stocks with Massive Potential
feed.summary: The metaverse market is projected to reach $5 trillion by 2030, with a significant majority of consumers and industry leaders anticipating positive impacts. This article highlights seven top metaverse stocks and ETFs, including Global X Metaverse ETF (VR), ProShares Metaverse ETF (VERS), Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF (METV), Meta Platforms (META), Nvidia (NVDA), Roblox (RBLX), and Unity Software (U), recommending them as key investment opportunities in this emerging sector. It notes that many of these stocks are currently oversold, presenting potential for future gains as the metaverse concept gains traction.

feed.title: Chinese DPU chip firm gains funds, unicorn status ...
feed.summary: Jaguar Microsystems, a Chinese Data Processing Unit (DPU) chip company founded in 2020 by former Broadcom executive Sunny Siu, has secured hundreds of millions of yuan in funding, propelling its valuation to unicorn status at approximately US$1.34 billion. The financing round was led by Tencent Holdings Ltd. and included other major investors. Jaguar Microsystems, which employs nearly 400 staff, released an FPGA version of its DPU in 2021 and plans for mass production of its system-chip version by 2023, primarily targeting cloud computing and internet companies, with Tencent expected to be a key customer.

feed.title: Finding NeMo: Sensory Taps NVIDIA AI for Voice and Vision Applications
feed.summary: Sensory, a pioneer in compact AI models for consumer electronics, is leveraging NVIDIA's NeMo toolkit and Triton Inference Server to enhance its voice and vision AI applications. This hybrid computing approach improves features like wake words and speech-to-text accuracy across billions of devices. The collaboration allows for more powerful and adaptable on-device models through cloud connections and over-the-air updates, supporting 17 languages and achieving superior word error rates.

feed.title: These 5 Semiconductor Suppliers Are Undervalued
feed.summary: The article highlights five undervalued semiconductor suppliers—ASML, Teradyne, Applied Materials, Lam Research, and KLA—that offer compelling long-term investment opportunities. Despite recent market downturns, these companies are crucial "arms dealers" in the semiconductor industry, poised to profit from continuous technological advancements and a highly concentrated market. Each company boasts a Wide Economic Moat designation from Morningstar, indicating strong competitive advantages and potential for sustained high returns.

feed.title: DDR5: How Faster Memory Speeds Shape The Future
feed.summary: This article discusses the advancements and challenges brought by DDR5 memory, which doubles the data rate of its predecessor, DDR4. It highlights how DDR5's increased speeds and power efficiency enable emerging technologies like IoT and V2X autonomous vehicles. The article also touches upon the future of DDR6, anticipating further speed increases and new signaling innovations to overcome physical limitations.

feed.title: Inferencing made simple with the NetApp DataOps Toolkit
feed.summary: NetApp has introduced new capabilities in its DataOps Toolkit for Kubernetes to simplify the deployment of Triton Inference Server with NetApp persistent storage. This advancement addresses the complexities of AI model inferencing, allowing data scientists and MLOps engineers to deploy Triton Inference Server instances with one simple command, leveraging NetApp's data fabric for seamless synchronization and enterprise-class data protection features like Snapshot copies. The integration aims to streamline the AI lifecycle, particularly for on-premises deployments or those requiring specific storage efficiencies and data sovereignty.

feed.title: Siemens and NVIDIA to Enable Industrial Metaverse
feed.summary: Siemens and NVIDIA announced an expanded partnership to create an industrial metaverse by connecting Siemens Xcelerator and NVIDIA Omniverse platforms. This collaboration aims to transform the manufacturing industry by enabling full-fidelity digital twins and integrating AI systems from edge to cloud. The goal is to accelerate the use of digital twins, improve productivity, and facilitate immersive, physics-based simulations for faster and more confident decision-making across product lifecycles.

feed.title: Building a Silicon Bulwark: How the United States and Taiwan Can Retain Joint Leadership of the Global Semiconductor Industry
feed.summary: This article examines how the United States and Taiwan can jointly maintain their leadership in the global semiconductor industry against challenges, particularly from China's talent poaching. It proposes three key areas for cooperation: strengthening mutual legal assistance, harmonizing export control approaches, and pooling investments in semiconductor R&D and fabrication. The goal is to fortify Taiwan's "silicon shield" into a broader transnational bulwark.
